wci.headline: WCI declined 3%, with diverging trends across the Asia–Europe and Transpacific trade lanes. See detailed commentary below.
wci.text_en:
Our detailed assessment for Thursday, 26 Nov 2026
The Drewry World Container Index (WCI), the benchmark widely referenced by procurement teams, decreased 3% to $4,032 per 40ft container this week, driven by lower rates on the Transpacific trade route amid weak demand.
On the Transpacific trade route, rates continued their downtrend for the eighth consecutive week. Spot rates from Shanghai to New York decreased 7% to $7,615 per 40ft container, and those from Shanghai to Los Angeles fell 8% to $6,437 per 40ft container. Amid weak demand, carriers are reducing capacity through blank sailings. According to Drewry's
Container Capacity Insight , seven blank sailings have been announced for next week, compared with five this week. Despite these capacity reductions, Drewry expects freight rates to decrease further next week.
On the Asia-Europe/Med trade route, spot rates from Shanghai to Genoa increased 8% to $4,802 per 40ft container, while Shanghai to Rotterdam rates remained the same for the second consecutive week at $3,485 per 40ft container. Carriers are managing capacity through blank sailings. According to Drewry’s
Container Capacity Insight , seven blank sailings (3 Asia-Europe, 4 Asia-Med) are announced for next week, higher than four (3 Asia-Europe, 1 Asia-Med) this week.
As demand is expected to strengthen in December ahead of the new contract season and upcoming CNY, many carriers have announced PSS of $1,000–$1,500 per 40ft container on the Asia–Europe trade route, along with higher FAK rates of $4,500–$4,600 per 40ft container for Asia to North Europe and $6,400–$6,800 per 40ft container for Asia to Med, effective 1 December. As a result, Drewry expects rates to increase in the coming weeks.
The East–West container freight market is showing diverging trends, with rates increasing on Asia–Med while declining on Transpacific trade routes amid easing demand. Demand is expected to strengthen on Asia–Europe/Med trade routes in December. Meanwhile, European port congestion and continued geopolitical uncertainty in the Strait of Hormuz remain key concerns.
Suez Canal transits have been increasing as more carriers resume Red Sea routings; last week, 60 vessels transited the canal. The immediate risk of a watchmen strike at Los Angeles/Long Beach has eased following a tentative agreement. Shippers should expect continued freight rate volatility in December, driven by demand fluctuations, capacity management, port congestion, and geopolitical developments.

paragraphs: 26 Kasım 2026 itibarıyla Drewry Dünya Konteyner Endeksi (WCI), zayıf talep ve Transpasifik hattındaki düşüşlerin etkisiyle %3 gerileyerek 40'lık konteyner başına 4.032 dolara indi. Şanghay–New York hattında fiyatlar %7 azalarak 7.615 dolara, Şanghay–Los Angeles hattında ise %8 düşerek 6.437 dolara geriledi. Buna karşın, Asya–Avrupa hattındaki Şanghay–Cenova navlun fiyatları %8 artışla 4.802 dolara çıkarken, Şanghay–Rotterdam fiyatları 3.485 dolarda sabit kaldı.

Aralık ayında talebin güçlenmesi beklenirken, taşımacılar Asya–Avrupa hattında ek zamlar duyurdu. Drewry, talep dalgalanmaları, kapasite yönetimi, liman yoğunluğu ve jeopolitik gelişmeler nedeniyle Aralık ayında navlun fiyatlarında dalgalanmaların sürmesini öngörüyor.
